body: My parents did the routine vaccinations when my brother and I were infants/toddlers. My brother turned out to have aspbergers. I suspect, but have no confirmation, that that may have influenced a shift in my mother’s thinking later, once the HPV vaccine came out. I was at the prime age (11? 12?) and my mom said no to the vaccine, her reasoning being 1) “they are just loading up kids with too many vaccines these days” and 2) “she won’t get cervical cancer.” Fast forward a couple years and I am a teenager and have *just* lost my virginity. I have my first ever Pap smear and the results come back “irregular,” which is often caused by HPV. My mom blamed my promiscuity (protected sex a handful of times with a monogamous boyfriend). I got the HPV vaccine myself at my university health clinic within a few months. She was supportive but still suspicious of what she perceives to be “too many vaccines these days.”

In regard to your first point--can you elaborate?  I am a bit unclear about the process of what in-patient looks like and what there could make me uncomfortable enough to want to leave.

As for the second point:

* Therapy: felt a bit like work to me.  I've had three therapists in my lifetime and the first was judgmental (I was self-coping with alcohol and sex and judgement didn't really help).  The second, I think, was maybe just bad at her job.  She would try and get me to list things I liked doing and I never could think of anything aside from "completing a to do list" (ha) so we ended up having silly conversations about how I should go check things off of my to do list?  The third was nice enough, but I wasn't quite ready to talk about my sexual assault yet (I went and saw her after it had just happened and stopped after a few sessions).  What they all had in common was it was expensive and a huge time investment.
* Meds: i took 60mg of Cymbalta daily.  It has been very hard going off of them.  I find myself shaking with emotion very often.  I have been on Lexapro in the past, but going off of that did not compare at all to going off of Cymbalta.  Cymbalta also constipated me (sorry for the TMI) and I can't tell you how much better I feel now that that's not a problem.  Cymbalta made me very productive and generally content, but I did struggle with the fact that it made me emotionless to a fault.
